metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor (Clarivate; publisher-reported)
metrics.population: Journal-level JIF: citations in 2025 to journal content published in 2023–2024, relative to the number of citable items published in 2023–2024. Raw numerator and denominator are not disclosed on the journal page.
metrics.note: The current official journal homepage labels this the 2025 Journal Impact Factor. The older official emeraldgrouppublishing.com page returned conflicting figures in search; the live migrated homepage is used. Citation impact is not acceptance difficulty or an individual paper's quality.

metrics.name: CiteScore (Scopus; publisher-reported)
metrics.population: Scopus CiteScore 2025: citations received in 2022–2025 to eligible documents published in 2022–2025, divided by those eligible documents (articles, reviews, conference papers, book chapters and data papers). Raw counts are not disclosed on the journal page.
metrics.note: Current official homepage explicitly labels 2025 CiteScore. This is the completed-year citation metric, not a tracker or an acceptance rate.

notes: Reviewed all 18 helper candidates and all three preceding fee, geography and AI policy files. Independently read Springer and Taylor & Francis AI policies, the Sage journal fee policy, WHO and Springer official journal metric pages; PAHO policy was blocked in web fetch and prior direct-page evidence is retained, not independently reconfirmed. Other role claims were examined for contradictions but not every underlying source was independently fetched.

Added current WHO Bulletin official 2025 impact factor and retained nine previously recorded Springer/Emerald measures. Empty metrics mean none verified during this review, not no metric exists. No acceptance rate inferred.

Taylor & Francis explicitly bars AI first drafts of manuscript sections; its prohibited classifications remain. Disclosure alone and silence do not establish substantive permission; unresolved fees and author eligibility remain unresolved. No remote writes or venue contact.
